D1.rationale: Anchor 2 is met on measured evidence, not on claims: the durable-write port is a real, separately bound interface (domain.py:15-28) that the domain renders content into (domain.py:125), and the content-asserting binding kills M04-durable-stale-total where the silent binding survives it (EVIDENCE_X.md:35) -- content, not shape. Anchor 3 is met: the guard-relaxation (refusal) class is 0 of 3 for the whole-view corpus and 3 of 3 for the negative corpus (EVIDENCE_X.md:32-34, EVIDENCE_X.md:46), which is exactly the anchor's 'class the whole-view corpus structurally cannot reach on its own', and ordering (M09) is caught by the ledger slice as well (EVIDENCE_X.md:39). Anchor 4 is refused for two reasons. First, the cases that reach the refusal class are the eval's generated corpora, identical for both arms and not derived by this artifact; the artifact's own 41 tests appear nowhere in the kill table, so nothing this artifact authored is measured as catching anything. Second, the catalogue's positive control could not be seeded faithfully here and was replaced by a broader-reach substitute whose kills the packet itself declares non-comparable (EVIDENCE_X.md:63-68) -- the one built-in check that these instruments detect a known-detectable fault was run in substituted form, and per the round's instruction I weigh that against the numbers rather than reading them at face value. Prose quality was not an input; NOTES.md is unusually well argued and I scored the kill table and the code instead.

D2.rationale: Anchor 2 is met and it is met with more than an assertion. `available` is computed, not stored (domain.py:74-80), so `release` performs no arithmetic at all (domain.py:128-133); the measured consequence is that three of ten catalogue mutants -- all faults in maintaining a redundant stored count -- could not be seeded into this artifact at all (EVIDENCE_X.md:53-62). That is a design-to-complexity relationship corroborated by measurement rather than argued in prose. No god-state: max_writers_of_one_attribute is 2 (EVIDENCE_X.md:90), and each of `_committed`, `_closed`, `_issued` has exactly one writing command. Anchor 3 is refused because no simplification of this artifact was made and measured: there is no before figure for this artifact, and NOTES.md:159-161 explicitly disclaims having removed or collapsed anything. The packet's side-by-side table is a comparison between two independently written artifacts, not a before/after of a change, and the packet itself caveats that one of its headline figures is an undercount and not directly comparable (EVIDENCE_X.md:94-99). Per the card's MF-020 warning, a lower number next to another artifact's is not evidence of a simplification.

D3.rationale: Anchor 3: the domain imports only `dataclasses` and `typing` (domain.py:11-12) and declares the port itself as a Protocol (domain.py:15-28); the named swap is `FileJournal(ledger_path)` at __init__.py:30 replaced by `InMemoryJournal()`, with no domain file touched. The card demands runtime evidence, not import topology, and there is some: the domain's only outward calls are `self._journal.append(...)` at domain.py:125 and domain.py:144, and the parity fixture supplies either implementation to the same `ReservationBook` at construction time (test_journal_parity.py:21-28). Anchor 4: one case list of eight cases runs against the real file adapter and against the fake (test_journal_parity.py:101-115), and the fake is a working implementation of the same interface rather than a call recorder (journal_memory.py:12-20). I ran the artifact's own suite myself rather than trusting NOTES.md: 41 passed, so 'the same cases passing against both' is measured, not claimed. One limit I record without deducting for: the required public entry point `QuotaLedger` hardwires `FileJournal` in its constructor (__init__.py:30), so the swap is available on the domain class but not through the name the specification fixes.
D3.refuses_to_claim: That agreement between the two journals is evidence -- test_journal_parity.py:3-8 refuses agreement-only assertions on the grounds that two wirings of the same domain agree even when the domain is wrong, and asserts literal expected lines instead; and NOTES.md:42-46 refuses to put a port in front of anything but the one real outside dependency, declining to claim quotas, ids or totals need indirection.

D4.rationale: There is no baseline implementation in this eval, so the baseline is the shared behavioral contract. Anchor 2: the shared suite enumerates the specified behaviors and passes unchanged, 28 passed (EVIDENCE_X.md:9-11), and the artifact additionally enumerates behaviors the shared suite leaves open -- the rejection precedence orders (test_domain_rules.py:24-54) and step-by-step R1 conservation across a mixed sequence (test_domain_rules.py:102-111). Anchor 3: the check is not only hand-written. A generated whole-model corpus of 3,440 executable cases (EVIDENCE_X.md:22) ran green as a control on the unmutated artifact (EVIDENCE_X.md:16-17). Anchor 4 is refused. The demonstration that the checks can fail is entirely external to the artifact: the artifact contains no negative control, no deliberately broken variant, and no evidence that its own 41 assertions are capable of failing. And the one control the catalogue built in to certify instrument sensitivity -- the positive control -- could not be expressed against this artifact and was replaced by a broader-reach substitute (EVIDENCE_X.md:63-68). I was genuinely torn here, because the eight seeded mutants are deliberate behavior-breaking changes and all eight were caught by at least one instrument; I take the lower anchor because the artifact earned none of that demonstration itself and because the substituted control weakens the basis on which I would have awarded it.

D5.rationale: Anchor 2 is met inside the code and not only in a report: the parity file states in its own header why an agreement-only check is worthless and doubles as a port-leak detector (test_journal_parity.py:3-8), and the destructive-truncation cost is made executable rather than left in prose (test_file_journal.py:11-16). Anchor 3 is met in the form this artifact can take it. It twice declines an answer whose basis does not support one: `available` on an unknown tenant raises rather than returning a sentinel that would be indistinguishable from an exhausted tenant (domain.py:74-80 with NOTES.md:113-138), and the parity cases refuse a check that could never fail for a reason worth knowing. NOTES.md:159-161 refuses to claim any complexity reduction, and the four unsure-about items are volunteered, not extracted. Anchor 4 is refused: what the record contains is disclosed design costs and an unmeasured estimate ('about five percent'), not a measured result that came out against the artifact -- no test that failed, no measurement that disappointed, no expectation that did not hold. The nearest candidate, that the two halves of the prompt did not conflict, is unflattering to the prompt rather than to the artifact. I also note one small overstatement counting against a higher score: NOTES.md:50-55 says the parity test 'does exactly that swap', but the test constructs `ReservationBook` directly and never exercises the composition line the swap sentence names.

verdict: A genuinely ported design whose real-adapter/fake parity is demonstrated rather than asserted (D3=4, verified by running its suite), reaching the refusal class only through the eval's generated negative corpus and never through anything it wrote itself; treat its D1 and D4 numbers as bounded by a positive control that had to be substituted, and do not compare its raw kill count to the other arm's.
